title: Forbidden Literature
next_chapter_hook: Chen Nian's figure vanished into the shadows of the Forbidden Grounds, leaving behind only words that shook one to the core—the sect's founding ancestor had not become the sect master of his own will. What secret lay hidden within? In the next chapter, a corner of the truth would be revealed.

text.content: The lamplight in the Scripture Repository swayed in the night wind. The sect keeper Elder's turbid eyeballs turned slightly, as if weighing something. Chen Ji noticed the old man's knuckles gripping the fly whisk had turned bone-white—a posture of forcibly suppressed fear. "The Forbidden Grounds..." The old man finally spoke, his voice pressed extremely low, "This old one has guarded this Scripture Repository for three hundred years, and never has anyone set foot there." He paused, his turbid gaze sweeping the surroundings, "What is stored there... are the founding ancestor's personally handwritten scriptures."

dialogue.content: The founding ancestor's personally handwritten scriptures?" Chen Ji's voice carried not a trace offluctuation, "Since these are the ancestor's handwritten texts, why are they sealed in the Forbidden Grounds? Is the Elder attempting to deceive me?"

text.content: The sect keeper Elder's lips quivered, the fly whisk trembling in his grasp. Chen Ji could see clearly—the old man was afraid, not of thistrash disciple, but of the secret within the Forbidden Grounds itself. In the lamplight, the old man's wrinkles cut deep like knife marks, each one a furrow of time. He opened his mouth as if to speak, yet ultimately could only shake his head.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji's fingertips gently brushed his sleeve, where his final trump card lay hidden. The Tianji Record Fragment warmed subtly beneath the fabric, as if sensing its master's intent. He did not act immediately, merely standing there, his gaze tranquil as stagnant water. This serenity was more unsettling than any threat—the sect keeper Elder's forehead beaded with fine sweat.

text.content: The sect keeper Elder's body stiffened violently, his turbid old eyes flashing a terrified expression. He stared at Chen Ji as if gazing upon an inconceivable being. "You... how do you know..." The words were half-spoken when he suddenly covered his mouth, as if realizing he'd nearly uttered something forbidden. The lamplight danced behind him, stretching his shadow into a grotesque, twisted form.

Chen Ji did not speak, merely withdrawing a yellowed fragment from his sleeve with deliberate slowness. The aura of the Tianji Record permeated the air, an indescribable heaviness as if threads of fate wove through the characters. The sect keeper Elder's face instantly drained of color. He stumbled back two steps, colliding with the bookshelf behind him, several ancient texts clattering to the floor. "T... Tianji Record..." His voice quavered almost incoherently, "You are from the Chen family..."

dialogue.content: Chen Ji returned the fragment to his sleeve, his voice maintaining its terrifying calm: "What does the Elder know? You might as well speak directly. I lack much patience." His gaze resembled an abyss, and the sect keeper Elder perceived within those eyes something cold that did not belong to atrash. The old man's defenses finally crumbled. His voice emerged hoarse, like sandpaper grinding: "The Forbidden Grounds... third level, seventh bookshelf, the innermost blood-red volume..."

text.content: Traversing through layers of bookshelves, Chen Ji finally arrived at the third level of the Forbidden Grounds. A faint sandalwood fragrance permeated the air, yet carried an ancient presence that chilled the heart. He found the seventh bookshelf, and in its depths, a handwritten manuscript lay quietly. The cover was blood-red, its corners inlaid with dark golden patterns—unmistakably the color of Chen bloodline. More诡异的是, not a speck of dust marred this manuscript—as if someone had just perused it.

choice.prompt: The manuscript lay before him, its faintly visible dark golden patterns on the cover pricking Chen Ji's eyes—those were marks of the Chen bloodline. Why would the founding ancestor use Chen bloodline colors to seal this text? What secrets lay within?

choices.description: Regardless of traps, since we've come there's no retreat. Truth lies before us—must charge forward even if dragon's pool and tiger's den await.
choices.visible_cost: May trigger formations, alerting the Scripture Keeper Elder
choices.risk_hint: The Forbidden Grounds may contain unknown formations

text.content: Chen Ji drew a deep breath, reaching for the blood-red manuscript. The instant it touched his hand, an icy sensation spread from his fingertips throughout his entire body, as if countless eyes watched him from the darkness. He steadied his composure, opening the first page—the calligraphy bold and powerful, carrying a profound vicissitude. However, when he glimpsed the first line, his heart suddenly skipped. "I, Chen Tiange, did not willingly accept the sect master position—compelled by heavenly mandate, my body not my own..."

choices.description: The aura here is too bizarre. Retreat first to consult with Mo Xiansheng, then plan. Strategic action before execution—that is the wisest course.
choices.visible_reward: Steadily advance, obtain Mo Xiansheng's analysis
choices.risk_hint: There may be a time limit

text.content: Chen Ji did not act rashly, but stepped back, gently sweeping the Tianji Record Fragment across the manuscript's cover. The characters on the fragment trembled slightly, as if resonating with some force. After a moment, he furrowed his brow—this manuscript bore some formation. If forcibly opened, it might trigger unknown alarms. He memorized this discovery, turned, and left the Forbidden Grounds, intending to first consult with Mo Xiansheng.

Chen Ji's heart raced. The founding ancestor—that legendary figure who had supposedly reversed fate with a mortal body and established the Tianqing Sect's eternal foundation—had actually written in his personal manuscript that he was "unwilling"? He steadied his composure, continuing to read. "I was merely an ordinary mortal, seeking the Dao and immortality, unwilling to stain my hands with worldly power. Yet heavenly cycles and fate compelled this—forcing the sect master position upon me. I exhausted my entire life's strength trying to break free, only to discover I was merely a chess piece in heaven's game..."

Chen Ji's pupils contracted violently. A chess game? Heaven's arranged chess game? He continued reading, only to find the subsequent content had been deliberately obliterated, the ink so heavy one could barely discern the original characters. Only the final line remained faintly legible: "...Should any descendant encounter this book, remember—the Tianji Record is not a blessing, but a curse. Those who control it will ultimately be devoured by fate. Learn from my downfall, descendants..."

dialogue.content: Chen Ji was still drowning in shock, when a voice suddenly sounded from behind him: "Brother, don't look any further." The voice was cold and clear with a hint of trembling. Chen Ji's whole body trembled. He spun around sharply, only to see a slender figure standing at the entrance of the forbidden grounds. Moonlight poured in from the high windows, illuminating the visitor's face—a face bearing a seven-point resemblance to Chen Ji, with a high bridge of the nose and a defined jawline, except the complexion was pale to the point of being translucent, as if it hadn't seen sunlight in years.

text.content: "Chen Nian." Chen Ji's voice was hoarse and almost unrecognizable. Seventeen years, he had searched for seventeen years, waking from nightmares countless nights, teetering on the edge of life and death countless times, all just to find this estranged sister. And now, she stood before him, alive and breathing, not a hallucination, not an enemy's trap. Moonlight shone on her, stretching her shadow long. She simply gazed at him quietly, tears glistening in her eyes.

dialogue.content: "Brother, I've finally waited for you." Chen Nian's voice was soft, as if afraid to disturb something. Her gaze fell on the handwritten manuscript in his hand, her expression complex. "You shouldn't have seen this. Before you're strong enough, these truths will kill you." Chen Ji didn't move, his eyes fixed on his sister's face, trying to find any flaw. But on that face there was only exhaustion and... fear? What was she afraid of?

choice.prompt: The sister he hadn't seen for seventeen years suddenly appeared in the forbidden grounds, the shocking secrets of the manuscript still in his hand—at this moment, Chen Ji faced a difficult choice. Should he believe Chen Nian's words and put down the manuscript, or continue investigating the truth?

choices.description: She is my only relative, I'm willing to give her a chance. Let me first hear what she has to say, the truth isn't going anywhere.
choices.visible_reward: Gain Chen Nian's trust, learn more about the situation
choices.process_label: set down manuscript look at Chen Nian

text.content: Chen Ji slowly placed the manuscript back where it was, his gaze always locked on his sister. "Nian Nian, how are you here? Where have you been all these years?" His voice was soft, yet carried undeniable seriousness. Chen Nian's eyes reddened, she stepped forward, but stopped three feet away from him. "Brother, people from the Holy Sect have been searching for me. They say I'm the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key'... I don't understand what that means, but I know my existence will bring danger to you."

choices.description: Her timing is too convenient, I can't trust anyone easily. First probe how much she knows, then decide.
choices.visible_reward: Gain more information, judge her stance

text.content: Chen Ji didn't put down the manuscript, instead guarding it behind his back, coldly looking at Chen Nian. "How do you know I'm here? What does this manuscript say, how much do you know?" A flash of hurt crossed Chen Nian's face, but she quickly suppressed her emotions. "Brother, you've changed. The old you wouldn't speak to me like this." She paused, "But it's fine, you're doing the right thing. In this world, the most unreliable thing is the human heart—including mine."

choices.description: The secrets in the manuscript I must know. Whatever she says, I must uncover this secret today.
choices.visible_cost: Might create conflict with my sister
choices.visible_reward: Uncover all the secrets of the manuscript

text.content: Chen Ji ignored Chen Nian's obstruction and directly opened the second half of the manuscript. Chen Nian let out a startled cry, but didn't step forward to stop him. The contents of the following pages were even more shocking—the words 'Heaven's Mandate Eye' appeared repeatedly throughout the text, along with extensive records of how seers throughout history were manipulated. And on the very last page, Chen Ji saw a name that made his blood run cold: 'Chen Xuan.' That was his father. The manuscript recorded that Chen Xuan didn't die from a cultivation accident, but was 'recycled' as a chess piece by the Heavenly Mandate Eye.

Chen Nian fell silent for a moment, moonlight casting a faint shadow across her face. She spoke, her voice as light as a sigh: "Brother, do you want to know why the founding ancestor said he was 'unwilling'?" She didn't wait for Chen Ji's answer, continuing on her own: "Because from the very beginning, he never willingly became the sect master. Every sect master was 'chosen'—chosen by Heaven, manipulated by fate. Their 'will' never mattered." Chen Ji's heart skipped a beat. "You mean..." His voice was hoarse. Chen Nian lifted her head, a flash of desolation in her eyes: "I mean—the founding ancestor was not a willing sect master."

The words struck like a sudden thunderclap, exploding in Chen Ji's mind. He unconsciously gripped the manuscript in his hand tightly, his knuckles turning white. The founding ancestor—that legendary figure, that revered and worshipped ancestor, was actually a puppet controlled by Heaven? What did this mean? Did it mean the entire history of the Tianqing Sect needed to be rewritten? Did it mean that his Tianji Record, his fate, had been arranged by someone from the very beginning?

dialogue.content: At this moment, the Tianji Record Fragment hidden in his sleeve suddenly grew warm, and an elderly voice rang out in Chen Ji's mind: "Young man, you've finally discovered it." It was Mo Xiansheng. "However, this is just the tip of the iceberg. The true secret is far more terrifying than you can imagine." Chen Ji suppressed the turbulent waves in his heart and asked mentally: What secret? Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a moment, his voice growing even more somber: "Have you ever thought about why you can see the future? Why the Tianji Record chose you? Heaven never does anything meaningless. It chose you, and there must be a purpose for it."

text.content: Chen Ji stood beneath the moonlight, the weight of the manuscript feeling like a thousand jun. The founding ancestor's testament, Chen Nian's appearance, Mo Xiansheng's hints... all the clues pointed toward a terrifying direction. The Eye of Heavenly Dao—this name appeared before him for the second time. He recalled the words on the Tianji Record Fragment that he had ignored: 'The fatal backlash of fate.' So from the beginning, he was not merely a lucky waste disciple. He was a chess piece, a chess piece meticulously placed by Heavenly Dao. And now, he was stepping into the center of that unknown chess game.

Chen Nian gazed at him quietly, a flicker of heartache passing through her eyes. 'Brother, I can't tell you too much. Some things, once spoken, will come true.' She paused, 'But I can tell you one thing—the Holy Sect has always been searching for me. They call me the 'Key to Heavenly Fate,' saying I can open a door that should remain closed. I don't know what that means, but I know my existence interferes with the Tianji Record's foresight.' Chen Ji's pupils slightly constricted. He recalled that when he previously used the Tianji Record, there were indeed some blurry visions—and in those visions, it seemed his sister was always present.

'Nian Nian.' Chen Ji finally spoke, his voice hoarse. Chen Nian raised her head, the moonlight illuminating her features—her face etched with exhaustion and vicissitudes. 'These years you...' Chen Ji wanted to ask, yet didn't know where to begin. Chen Nian gently shook her head, cutting him off: 'Brother, now is not the time for reunions.' She stepped back, her form beginning to fade into the shadows of the forbidden zone. 'There are more secrets in this manuscript, but your current strength isn't enough to bear them. When you're ready, come find the answers.' Chen Ji instinctively wanted to chase after her, yet found his legs rooted to the spot, immovable.

'Brother.' Chen Nian's voice drifted from the shadows, carrying a tremor. 'Regardless of whether you believe me or not, I will stand on your side. Because... you are my brother.' Her voice faded, her silhouette completely vanished into the darkness. The Scripture Depository returned to silence, only the moonlight continued to spill. Chen Ji stood in place, the manuscript in his hand impossibly heavy. He didn't pursue her—not from unwillingness, but because he knew his sister was right; the time wasn't right.

Chen Ji drew a deep breath, carefully tucking the manuscript into his sleeve. Mo Xiansheng's voice emerged once more: 'Lad, that girl speaks truly. 'Key to Heavenly Fate'... if this old man hasn't miscalculated, her existence can obstruct the Tianji Record's foresight, possibly even interfering with Heavenly Dao itself. That's why the Holy Sect has ceaselessly pursued her.' Chen Ji remained silent, standing motionless as night wind brushed his face. Beneath the moonlight, his gaze was profound and unfathomable.

The Tianji Record, Xuanwu Sect, Tianqing Sect, Demonic Path, Holy Sect, Chen Nian, Mo Xiansheng... all the clues wove together, pointing toward a truth growing increasingly clear yet simultaneously obscure. Chen Ji paced out of the Scripture Depository, night wind kissed his face with a trace of chill. He gazed upward at the sky, starlight brilliant, yet seemed an invisible eye constantly observing him. 'Eye of Heavenly Dao...' he murmured to himself, voice barely audible, 'What exactly do you intend for me?' Night wind howled past, and no one answered his question.

Chen Ji's pace didn't falter, yet his thoughts were already racing at lightning speed. The secrets within the manuscript, his sister's warning, Mo Xiansheng's implication... everything converged on a singular truth—he wasn't playing chess; he was being played. The Tianji Record Fragment in his sleeve faintly radiated warmth, as if resonating with his contemplation. His lips curved slightly, a meaningful smile emerging. 'Very well, very good.' he said softly, his tone devoid of any discernible emotion. 'Since Heavenly Dao wishes to play chess, then I shall play until the end.' He raised his head, starlight falling upon that composed face, revealing a deeply concealed sharpness. Seventeen years of arrangement had only just begun.

Gazing back toward the Scripture Depository, Chen Ji's expression deepened. The cover of that blood-red manuscript still lingered in his mind—the founding ancestor's personal testament, concealing secrets sufficient to overturn Tianqing Sect's ten-thousand-year foundation. He deeply etched this discovery into memory, interweaving it with Mo Xiansheng's existence and his sister's warning. The Eye of Heavenly Dao, prophecies from generations past, manipulated destiny... every clue pointed toward a chilling truth. He wasn't playing chess; he was inherently part of the chess game. Yet since he had already entered the game, there was only one path—to continue until the very end.
